742170101.text: ...We have to go, right this instant!

742170102.text: Calm down, Garcia. Didn't Officer Menthe say that things in Petrichor have returned to normal?

742170103.text: Sir, please, have faith in the good gentlemen of the Club. They are brilliant people, they will be fine, the threat notwithstanding.

742170104.text: Yes, yes, I know Babisse is very clever, and that Mécantre always has a strategy handy, but neither of them is good at dealing with malicious intent!

742170105.text: I sent them letters to warn them, but that despicable merchant was far too cunning for them!

742170106.text: Ah! The humanity! Good folk are always being taken advantage of by the bad!

742170107.text: In that case, we can only put our faith in Mr. Bossuet, and hope that the Fontaine Research Institute can see the Club members through.

742170108.text: See the Daydream Club itself blown sky-high, more like... Ugh...

742170111.text: #Ah, my dear {NICKNAME}, you're here at last! Wondrous, wondrous! Come, let us be off, immediately!

742170112.text: #Good to see you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. You've been doing well, I can tell.

742170113.text: Hey there, Kaia! Hehe, is it just Paimon, or did you get prettier since we last saw you?

742170114.text: Hmm, we do have a poem in Liyue. How does it go now? Something like...

742170115.text: I think I remember... "Even in fields a-flower, mine eyes dither to stray"... Something like that? It was in an anthology I read once.

742170116.text: Thank you, Lutong, Liyue truly is a comprehensive repository of poetic wonders! In which case, let us depart — in the name of said wonders!

742170118.text: H—Hardly! I was simply... too warm! Yes! So worrisome were the wind and waves that I wore a few extra layers. Hahaha!

742170119.text: Is that so? Y'know, Paimon couldn't tell just by looking.

742170120.text: Pfft. Alright, everyone, let's go. Everything is ready.

742170121.text: My apologies, Mr. Garcia. I would have gotten you a few layers more if only we had known that you were so afraid of the cold.

742170122.text: In that case, please head to Petrichor first. I'll be waiting for some colleagues here first, and we will join you shortly.

742170201.text: Ah... Petrichor! My homeland, how lovely, how familiar, how...

742170202.text: Quiet... Sir, is your hometown famed for its tranquility?

742170203.text: Of course not. Babisse and Mécantre make all manner of crash and clamor every day, never mind anyone else...

742170204.text: Wait... Mécantre, Babisse... We must go to the Club first. Come with me, quickly!

742170205.text: ...Was that real? Or just an illusion? I—I saw it...

742170207.text: I... Wh—What have I done... Oh, Archons help us...

742170208.text: Mécantre! Babisse! I saw what happened at the Club, and feared something must've happened to you! Where's Este? What about Grispan?

742170209.text: Garcia!? I must be dreaming... or have I always been? What brings you back here?

742170210.text: You're... Remuria... No, no, no! Archons, my mind's just filled with this stuff, isn't it...

742170212.text: ...Grundeland. Just what are you up to this time? Find another opportunity to exploit? Or are you trying to take credit for our research again?

742170213.text: I... Well, I had considered doing so before, but...

742170214.text: Ah, so this is the fellow who coveted your research?

742170215.text: That's right! That's him. He hired people to tail us, and even sent them to search my room, trying to take the Numbering Machine for himself.

742170216.text: It hardly surprises me that you would wait for me in Petrichor once you realized that you wouldn't get anything out of me. I'll have you know, I already wrote a letter...

742170217.text: One moment, Garcia. He doesn't quite look right...

742170218.text: #Paimon would say that about everyone here, {NICKNAME}... C—Could it be that...

742170221.text: Wait, you mean that they also had that dream and became... other Remurians too?

742170223.text: R—Right. If they've been on this island the whole time, then Phobos would have...

742170224.text: I... That was exactly what I was thinking, Garcia. I confess, I was once an awful villain, and I...

742170225.text: So, good sir, I assume you planned to lure him over to Petrichor, before using the noble sentiments of these friends of yours here to influence him?

742170301.text: ...This research... big money... a pleasant collaboration. Trust me!

742170302.text: The Club's original purpose... provide for free... Research belongs to everyone...

742170303.text: Work with me... provide to more people... Professional business channels...

742170401.text: We can't convince everyone... lots of research results...

742170402.text: ...As long as you cooperate... I guarantee. First... maximum dividends...

742170403.text: ...Become the wealthiest researcher... Research whatever you want...

742170501.text: ...Stupid researchers... not even a ten-thousandth of your intelligence...

742170502.text: Cooperation... Mora... big business... doesn't work out, we'll just have to make him suffer some...

742170505.text: (A few dull thuds can be heard from the phonograph, and afterward, no more speaking can be heard.)

742170701.text: Thank you, kind lady... But I'm still feeling quite dizzy...

742170702.text: See? I told you it would work. They're looking much better already.

742170703.text: In that case, you should take the opportunity to recover.

742170704.text: Before the Gardes come to recover you, at any rate.

742170705.text: That's right, that's right! We've got evidence proving that you're a bad guy right here!

742170706.text: Thank Petrichor, you're back! Did you get those phonographs?

742170707.text: Of course, sir. Our plan worked. Babisse recorded this all-too-clever fellow's words down in full. It's all here in the phonographs.

742170708.text: You... You misunderstand. I shan't deny that I did terrible deeds in the past. I'm a scoundrel, rotten to the bone! I simply wish to redeem myself!

742170709.text: ...Ms. Kaia, did you put some kind of special Sumeru shrooms in your soup? You know, the sort that might make people want to turn their lives around in the blink of an eye?

742170710.text: No, I just made a pot of some simple fish soup. No spices, either, just salt.

742170712.text: Thank you, though... I suspect such charms as I have would only work on one person.

742170715.text: What are you up to this time, Grundeland? I've warned you...

742170716.text: The Daydream Club's research will not be used to make a single Mora! We are researchers, not money-grubbing louts!

742170717.text: Garcia, please wait... I... I'm willing to put a little faith in his desire to better himself.

742170718.text: I agree. We should at least give him a chance.

742170719.text: Alright, it seems that things are getting complicated. Let us take all of you to see a doctor first, shall we?

742170720.text: No, no, Garcia, listen to me. We... We experienced a huge collective dream.

742170721.text: In said dream, we had turned into stone statues, yet we weren't fully so. We could still think, see, and hear.

742170722.text: I could feel that someone else was in that stone statue besides me.

742170723.text: I could see through his eyes and hear through his ears, and think along with him through his soul... I was him, yet not him!

742170724.text: Me too... I felt that the person with me was a good person full of ideals and intelligence, who was constantly doing research and work, though not for himself.

742170725.text: He was following someone as a musician does a conductor's baton, but he never once noticed it. What... a terrifying life to have led. Ohhh...

742170726.text: #Uh oh, {NICKNAME}. When he says "conductor's baton," do you think he means...

742170714.text: Eh, this town's pretty, sure, but not that pretty...

742170801.text: I never imagined that my first diving trip would be in search of a city I glimpsed in a dream. How fascinating.

742170802.text: True, and one that has been sundered from the present for who knows how long, at that. It should have long since been buried in time...

742170803.text: ...Though we haven't found that city yet, this... bell is making quite the impression already.

742170804.text: Babisse, do you find anything around here familiar?

742170805.text: No, sorry... We were in a certain room at that time, and we couldn't move at all.

742170807.text: Stone statues? But according to you, those statues had a different consciousness within them, right? So you were like...

742170808.text: Like the statue's shadow, transcending time, space, and dreamscapes alike... Ah, a shame that I did not have that dream myself.

742170809.text: Milady, if you had turned into a statue's shadow, I fear Mr. Garcia and I would have no choice but to interview every stone in Fontaine.

742170810.text: *cough* Anyway, let's continue onward for now and look for your statue, alright, Mécantre?

742170811.text: ...It's right there! Up ahead! I remember now. I passed this way!

742170812.text: Hey, hey, Grundeland! Stop right there, you dratted—!

742170813.text: #{NICKNAME}! Please go with Mécantre and the others. I'll get a hold of Grundeland!

742170814.text: Yes, Sir. I will keep an eye on Ms. Kaia... As I would have, even if you had not managed to ask me to in time.

742170815.text: #Pfft... Nice to see that he's in such high spirits. In that case, {NICKNAME}, let us go on ahead.

742170816.text: With any luck, Mécantre's statue won't be too hard to find.

742171001.text: ...It's you. Yes, I know it! I dreamed of you.

742171003.text: That's right. In the dream, I was his "shadow."

742171004.text: He seemed to have been studying something known as a "high-altitude aqueduct." Even as a statue, he was constantly going over the details of its engineering.

742171005.text: How to lay it down across complex terrain, what materials to use, the length and width of said waterway...

742171006.text: That was what made him happy in life... He did not need to think of anything else.

742171007.text: And there I was, thinking about some strange aquabus design. It was... It was true happiness.

742171008.text: He was pondering an aquabus's specifications, style, and the time required to build it...

742171009.text: Huh, still together despite turning into statues? Guess you guys really are fated in some weird way...

742171012.text: I respect their love for their research, but at the same time, I felt sad for them.

742171013.text: I too, salute and mourn him.

subQuests.subQuestName: Return to the shore and talk to everyone

742171301.text: It's you... Yes, it's you. The person in my dream.

742171302.text: You... You were the director of the Remurian Academy of Sciences, in charge of all research projects. All was orderly, all went well, and it was true happiness...

742171303.text: Huh. Hang on a moment. Why are you all repeating the phrase "true happiness"?

742171304.text: It's nice liking your research and all, but most people wouldn't emphasize it as being "true happiness." There's... something creepy about all this...

742171305.text: But that's exactly what the person in the statue kept emphasizing to themselves, and they wholeheartedly believed in it.

742171308.text: He was a good man. Even after becoming a statue, he continued to worry about the other researchers, fret about unfinished research projects, and blamed himself for the latter...

742171309.text: But something was not right... and I just couldn't say what! And only once I'd awakened did Mr. Babisse tell me what was off.

742171310.text: They were so focused on research that they never once spared a thought for themselves!

742171311.text: This good person was just like all the others in their statues. They had no freedom. They just followed the invisible conductor's baton around.

742171312.text: How did you know that they didn't have any control?

742171313.text: That's right. You didn't know about Phobos at first, did you?

742171314.text: Well, we found something that they were missing.

742171315.text: What they were missing was a "daydream." This is something that no researcher should lack.

742171501.text: No, no, I'm not... I won't become the person who tormented you. No, never, never... *sobs*

742171503.text: To have seen someone's life in a dream, before returning to reality and understanding the pain that person went through...

742171504.text: Then finding out that what you thought was a dream was, in fact, real, and the life you bore witness to was also real...

742171507.text: *sigh* I'll go make something to drink. Mind helping me out, Garcia?

742171508.text: I'll be there. Lutong, watch over Grundeland, will you? If it turns out that his madness is an act...

742171509.text: In that case, sir, I will make it so he need not feign pain.

742171510.text: That said, you two look like you're doing just fine, Babisse, Mécantre.

742171511.text: We've just seen many people in our line of work trapped in similar situations.

742171512.text: Although this is the first time I've seen such... direct control.

742171513.text: As to why Grundeland reacted so strongly, we have a theory that comes from a more... sentimental perspective.

742171514.text: They say that the "despicable have their eyes closed." Grundeland used various methods to keep people under his thumb...

742171515.text: ...But he had never before taken note of or personally experienced what it was like to be controlled.

742171516.text: This time, he was forced to experience that pain for himself.

742171517.text: And the ordeal seems to have made quite the impression.

742175101.text: What has happened to the town? Did that idiot Grispan hypnotize everyone!?

742175102.text: But wait, where has he gone!? And he's taken Grobel with him, too... It couldn't really have been him, though, could it...?

742175103.text: Please, Mécantre, Babisse, come to your senses! The Club is counting on you!

742175104.text: Calm down, Garcia. Let's go make them some soup first. A little something warm will help them recover their wits.

742175105.text: Oh, alright... I really don't know what to do, Kaia. This is all a mess.

742175106.text: Don't worry, Dear, it's alright. You've got me, and that's not in doubt, is it?

742175201.text: That's right. You just couldn't learn to "daydream"... There's no lack of reality all around us. You just lacked that power to dream...

742175202.text: You have to... We have to look up at the sky and cease obsessing over Mora and tall towers. An empty space is where a researcher truly belongs...

742175301.text: Ah, there is truly no hope for me... Why did I... Oh, Archons, why did I do those things...

742175302.text: I'm just like that person. I wanted to pull the strings. Let others do my bidding. No... No, no, no...

742175401.text: Fish... Ah, yes, that's right. This is the fish I discovered most recently...

742175501.text: I only hope that we won't run into any trouble...

742175502.text: I hope so too, milady. As such, please stand behind us, and keep your distance from the water's edge.

742175601.text: The high-altitude waterway... What a wonderful idea... Yes, wondrous indeed.

742175701.text: The aquabus... Your designs were exquisite. Of that I have no doubt.

742179901.text: The group quickly sets out on the road to Petrichor...

742179902.text: You and Garcia work together to move the statue onshore...

742179903.text: "Provide for free," hmm? Heh. A respectable virtue indeed.

742179904.text: It seems that he still hasn't figured out why the Daydream Club exists... A shame, I suppose.

742179905.text: It appears evident that some accident occurred before they finished their conversation. A mixed blessing, as they say.
